questions.question: Why have traditional SPAs struggled with SEO?

options.text: Because content is rendered client-side via JS, which crawlers may not execute in time

questions.explanation: Crawlers that don't fully execute JS (or time out) see an empty shell, so JS-rendered content may not be indexed.

questions.question: SSR (Server-Side Rendering) helps SPA SEO by:

options.text: Sending pre-rendered HTML so crawlers see content immediately

questions.explanation: SSR (e.g. Angular Universal) returns full HTML from the server, making content visible to crawlers and improving first paint.

questions.question: What is the tradeoff between SSG and SSR?

options.text: SSG builds static HTML at build time (fast, great for fixed content); SSR renders per-request (fresh, dynamic)
SSG requires a database per request

questions.explanation: SSG pre-renders at build time (ideal for blogs/docs); SSR renders on each request (ideal for personalized/dynamic pages).

questions.question: Why is structured data (schema.org JSON-LD) valuable for SEO?

options.text: It lets search engines show rich results (ratings, breadcrumbs, FAQs)

questions.explanation: JSON-LD structured data helps Google produce rich snippets (Article, Product, FAQ), improving visibility/CTR.

questions.question: How do you set per-route <title> and meta tags in an Angular SPA?

options.text: Using the Title and Meta services, often with a route resolver/guard
They cannot be changed per route

questions.explanation: Angular's Title/Meta services update document head dynamically per route; with SSR this is also sent server-side.

questions.question: A canonical URL (rel="canonical") is used to:

options.text: Tell search engines which version of a URL is the authoritative one (avoid duplicate content)

questions.explanation: Canonical tags consolidate duplicate/similar URLs so ranking signals point to one preferred page.

questions.question: Social media preview cards (Open Graph) require:

options.text: OG meta tags in the served HTML head (needs SSR/prerender for SPAs)

questions.explanation: og:title/og:image etc. must be present in the HTML the social scraper fetches — so SPAs need SSR/prerender for correct previews.

questions.question: Core Web Vitals influence SEO because they measure:
questions.explanation: LCP, INP, CLS measure real UX; Google uses them as ranking signals. Use Lighthouse to monitor.
